message.content: 250. "The fire must be taken from beneath the retort as soon as the distillation is finished, not only to prevent the effect of the gaseous vapours, which will continue slowly to escape, from acting on the sides of the tub, but likewise to difpose the retorts or bodies to receive a quantity of warm water, which is to be poured in up to the neck. There is no reason to fear an excess of quantity, and the hotter the vessels are the better. It is essential, however, that it be not poured in cold, for fear of breaking the glass. The adopter is then to be unloosed from the neck of the leaden tube, if the operator chooses; and in order that no vapour may escape into the workshop, a bit of lute or a cork may be applied to the beak of the adopter. The sand bath easily permits the retort to be raised and returned again to its place, as well as the application of the lute or flopper to the neck of the adopter, this last being raised with one hand while the cork is put in with the other.
